title: Latham & Watkins: Harvey Firmwide Deployment and AI Academy
pub: Harvey AI / Latham & Watkins / Artificial Lawyer
author: Harvey Team · Latham & Watkins · Artificial Lawyer

dom.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility

st.t: Agentic infrastructure: Harvey tests vertical vendor durability
st.an: The source supports Harvey’s role as a test case for specialised legal-AI infrastructure by documenting a major firmwide enterprise licence, broad intended availability and a concrete training target. It also fits the synthesis’s caution: the announcement describes planned deployment and uses, but provides no measured adoption, accuracy, workflow, client-value or economic outcomes.
qs: by Harvey Team•Aug 11, 2025  Harvey is pleased to announce that Latham & Watkins LLP, one of the world’s leading law firms with a track record for excellence and innovation, has signed an enterprise license for firmwide rollout of the Harvey platform and its full suite of generative AI solutions.

Offering the most sophisticated AI platform in the market, Latham’s deployment aims to have all attorneys trained and operational by the end of the year, with attorneys leveraging the suite of AI solutions for various aspects of legal work, including research, document analysis, drafting, and more.

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source supports the platform-led expansion and competition narrative by treating firmwide deployments as strategically important wins that tend to create multi-year vendor–firm relationships. It provides evidence of Legora competing for leading firms, but does not address whether deployment produces productivity, accuracy or client outcomes, nor the need for selected workflows and training.
qs: Well, as noted by AL with other client wins of this kind, every major law firm that brings in a firmwide AI productivity platform like this, tends to mean a multi-year relationship.
Rivals, including Legora, are also going after the same law firms – as although there are millions of lawyers in the world, the top firms are the most sought after customers.

st.t: Power users: Usage volume may obscure value
st.an: Latham’s announcement is consistent with the cluster’s distinction between purchasing access and operational adoption: it pairs a firmwide licence with a target to train attorneys and use Harvey in defined legal tasks. However, it reports planned deployment rather than sustained engagement, workflow redesign, effective use or measured value, so it supports the proposition without materially extending its evidence base.

st.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility
st.an: Latham’s firmwide licence and planned rollout provide strong evidence of enterprise purchasing and institutional commitment, while the training target, undisclosed licence fee and absence of measured productivity or performance results reinforce the cluster’s distinction between commercial traction and proven operational value or durable defensibility.

kp.k: Enterprise licence extends Harvey across lawyers and business professionals
kp.d: Harvey's 11 August 2025 announcement reports that Latham & Watkins signed an enterprise licence for firmwide rollout of its full generative AI suite. The planned deployment covers more than 3,600 attorneys globally and business professionals supporting legal services; the announcement describes intended availability rather than demonstrated usage.
qs: has signed an enterprise license for firmwide rollout of the Harvey platform and its full suite of generative AI solutions.
The large-scale deployment will make Harvey widely available across the firm’s more than 3,600 attorneys globally, as well as business professionals that support the delivery of legal services.

kp.k: Attorney training and operational readiness targeted for year-end 2025
kp.d: Harvey states a goal of training all Latham attorneys and making them operational by the end of 2025, with applications including research, document analysis and drafting. This is a rollout objective, not a reported completion or measured productivity result.
qs: Latham’s deployment aims to have all attorneys trained and operational by the end of the year, with attorneys leveraging the suite of AI solutions for various aspects of legal work, including research, document analysis, drafting, and more.

kp.k: Leadership positions AI investment across delivery and business operations
kp.d: In customer quotations carried by Harvey, CIO Rene Mendoza describes Harvey as an addition to Latham's existing technology strategy, while COO LeeAnn Black commits to continued significant investment in generative AI and advanced technologies. Black frames transformation of both legal service delivery and business operations as the investment's purpose, rather than reporting quantified effects.
qs: We have consistently championed the integration of emerging technologies and AI throughout our business, and Harvey not only supports these goals but also accelerates them

We will continue to make significant investments in generative AI and advanced technology solutions as part of our comprehensive innovation strategy, driving transformation in both legal service delivery and business operations, while maintaining our commitment to excellence and superior client service

kp.k: AI Academy embeds practical training in associate development
kp.d: Latham's October 2024 announcement describes a multi-event AI Academy launched with a two-day, in-person Washington D.C. event for first- through fourth-year associates. Developed jointly by the AI Task Force, Training and Career Enhancement Committee and Technology Department, it uses practical training to support junior and midlevel associates at the intersection of AI, legal practice and business.
qs: Latham’s AI Academy comprises multiple events and training programs throughout the year aimed at different groups, including an inaugural two-day in-person training event for a group of first-through fourth-year associates.
The multi-pronged AI Academy was developed through a collaboration between Latham’s AI Task Force, Training and Career Enhancement (TACE) Committee, and Technology Department.
Sessions employed hands-on and skills-based training to support junior and midlevel associates with cutting-edge expertise in their practice.
Latham hosted a two-day training event in Washington D.C. to launch the firm’s AI Academy.

kp.k: AI literacy framed as necessary across practice areas
kp.d: Latham partner Fiona Maclean predicts AI will affect every area of law and argues that understanding AI is essential for future lawyers regardless of industry focus. Director of AI and Innovation John Scrudato describes practice transformation through routine-task automation and sophisticated analytics and insights. These are practitioner assertions motivating training, not measured findings about task displacement.
qs: AI will impact every area of law in the future. Whether an associate builds a practice in the tech sector or another industry across Latham’s global platform, understanding AI and the ever-evolving tech landscape is crucial for the next generation of legal professionals.
In addition to AI’s impact on our client’s businesses, AI is transforming the practice of law, from automating routine tasks to providing sophisticated analytics and insights.

kp.k: Academy extends beyond junior associates and internal audiences
kp.d: Latham describes ongoing virtual AI-and-law training available to lawyers at all levels and in any practice area, supplemented by presentations tailored to clients, educators and other legal-community audiences. The Academy therefore encompasses broader professional and client education as well as associate development.
qs: Latham lawyers at all levels and in any practice area can access AI Academy trainings and materials on a range of key topics.
AI Academy also provides custom presentations and trainings tailored to specific audiences, including clients, educators, and other members of the legal community.

kp.d: The Latham insights page titled "2025 AI Academy," dated 15 January 2026, reports that the annual immersive, skills-based programme welcomed over 400 associates. Its statement concerns participation and intended preparation for AI's business impact, rather than a measured assessment of learning or subsequent performance.
qs: Our annual immersive, skills-based AI Academy welcomed over 400 associates, equipping them with the knowledge and tools to navigate the transformative impact of artificial intelligence on global businesses.

kp.k: Large-firm contracts intensify competition among AI platform vendors
kp.d: Artificial Lawyer characterises Latham as a significant customer win, citing revenues over $7 billion, more than 3,600 lawyers and Harvey's reported 42 AmLaw 100 customers, including Latham. The publication says the licence fee is unknown and anticipates a notable revenue boost; it argues that firmwide platforms tend to create multi-year relationships. It identifies Legora as a competitor pursuing the same sought-after firms and reports its 2025 wins at Cleary Gottlieb, Mishcon de Reya and BCLP.
qs: Latham is the second-largest firm in the US, with revenues over $7 billion and more than 3,600 lawyers.
Harvey recently mentioned they had 42 of the AmLaw 100 as customers – and Latham is one of them.
We don’t know what the licence fee is, but a deal for so many lawyers and staff will clearly be a notable revenue boost for Harvey.
every major law firm that brings in a firmwide AI productivity platform like this, tends to mean a multi-year relationship.
Legora meanwhile this year has signed another leading US law firm: Cleary Gottlieb, and also several UK-based firms including Mishcon de Reya and BCLP.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Harvey's team announces large-scale AI availability at Latham for research, document analysis, drafting and other legal work.
pts.d: The Harvey Team's 11 August 2025 announcement states that Latham signed an enterprise license covering its full suite of generative AI solutions. The proposed rollout makes the platform widely available to more than 3,600 attorneys globally and supporting business professionals, with a goal of all attorneys being trained and operational by year-end. This describes deployment and intended lawyer use, not demonstrated productivity gains or autonomous replacement of lawyers.

pts.k: Latham executives present AI investment as accelerating technology integration and transforming legal service delivery and business operations.
pts.d: Chief Information Officer Rene Mendoza says Harvey supports and accelerates Latham's existing technology and AI integration goals. Chief Operating Officer LeeAnn Black commits to continued investment in generative AI and advanced technologies as part of a transformation strategy that also maintains client-service standards. These are executive statements of strategic direction rather than quantified outcome findings.

pts.k: Latham speakers predict profession-wide relevance of AI knowledge and describe AI as already changing legal tasks.
pts.d: In the October 2024 Academy announcement, partner Fiona Maclean predicts that AI will affect every area of law and makes AI understanding a professional-development requirement regardless of sector. Director of AI and Innovation John Scrudato describes current changes ranging from routine-task automation to sophisticated analytics and insights. Partner Michael Rubin frames training as equipping both technology-focused and other associates for an increasingly AI-integrated world.

pts.k: Latham presents its AI Academy as a means of developing practice-relevant skills and preparing lawyers to advise AI-affected businesses.
pts.d: Latham's October 2024 announcement describes hands-on training, ongoing virtual materials and audience-specific training as responses to AI's effects on legal practice and clients' businesses. Scrudato says lawyers can acquire skills usable in practice. The '2025 AI Academy' page, published on 15 January 2026, reports participation by over 400 associates and characterizes the program as equipping them to navigate AI's business impact.

pts.k: Artificial Lawyer argues that firmwide AI contracts are strategically important vendor wins because elite-firm customers generate revenue and tend to enter multi-year relationships.
pts.d: Artificial Lawyer's 11 August 2025 article characterizes Latham's adoption as a significant revenue and market-share win for Harvey, the legal-AI vendor. It reports Harvey's statement that 42 AmLaw 100 firms were customers, including Latham, and describes competition with Legora for sought-after leading firms. The article qualifies its revenue inference by acknowledging that the license fee is unknown and describes multi-year relationships as a tendency, not a disclosed term of this contract.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: Deployment and training claims rest on organizational announcements; transformation claims rest on speakers' authority and descriptions of intended use.
pts.d: Harvey reports the signed enterprise license and intended population of more than 3,600 attorneys plus support professionals. Harvey CEO Winston Weinberg refers to Latham's extensive evaluation, but the document supplies no evaluation methods or results. Latham describes the Academy's curriculum, two-day inaugural event and institutional collaborators, and later reports over 400 associate participants. These establish reported activities and scale; no task-performance measurements, client outcomes, cost savings or measured training gains are provided. Claims of platform sophistication and training uniqueness are promotional assertions without comparative evidence in the supplied text.

pts.k: Artificial Lawyer supports its market interpretation with firm scale, vendor-reported customer counts and examples of rival contracts.
pts.d: The article cites Latham's reported position as the second-largest US firm, revenues exceeding $7 billion and more than 3,600 lawyers. It attributes the 42-of-the-AmLaw-100 customer figure to Harvey and lists Legora wins at Cleary Gottlieb, Mishcon de Reya and BCLP. Its expectation of substantial vendor revenue and multi-year customer relationships is an editorial inference from contract scale and other client wins; no license price, contract duration or systematic retention data is supplied.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The sources distinguish an end-2025 rollout goal, ongoing training and investment, and open-ended forecasts about professional change.
pts.d: The August 2025 Harvey announcement targets all attorneys being trained and operational by the end of 2025; it does not report achievement of that target. The Academy launched in October 2024 with multiple events and ongoing virtual training. The page titled '2025 AI Academy' is dated 15 January 2026 and retrospectively reports participation, not completion of Harvey training. Maclean's every-area-of-law prediction has no deadline; Scrudato describes automation and analytics as current changes. Black's investment commitment is ongoing. Artificial Lawyer's multi-year relationship claim is a general tendency conditional on major firms adopting firmwide platforms, rather than confirmation of this deal's duration.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claims concern Latham's lawyers and support staff, clients across industries, broader training audiences and competing legal-AI vendors.
pts.d: The rollout covers Latham's global attorney population and business professionals supporting service delivery. Initial in-person Academy training targets first- through fourth-year associates; broader training serves lawyers at all levels and across practices, with custom offerings for clients, educators and the legal community. Clients are portrayed as businesses needing advice as AI becomes integrated into operations. The vendor-market claims concern Harvey and competitors such as Legora competing for leading law firms, including AmLaw 100 customers. The document does not predict staffing reductions, changed billing arrangements or expanded access to justice.
